# Introduction {background-color="#a13c65"}

## Purpose of This Report

-   Employees Federal Credit Union (EFCU) wants to know why members are not borrowing from the credit union and how members view its operations.
-   This report summarizes the analysis for four research questions:
    -   **R1:** Why do people join the Credit Union?
    -   **R2:** Why do members use other financial institutions when they need to borrow funds?
    -   **R5:** How well are the members aware of the services offered by the credit union?
    -   **R6:** What are the members' attitudes and beliefs about how effectively the credit union is operated?
-   Data: 128 survey respondents (mail survey, simple random sample of 300 members).

## Data Analysis Plan

| RQ | Variables | Scale | Test |
|:--|:----------|:------|:-----|
| R1 | q7r (savings rates) | Interval | Descriptives, one-sample t-test (μ = 3) |
| R2 | q8r (loan rates), q30 (CU rates lower than others) | Interval | Descriptives, one-sample t-test (μ = 3) |
| R5 | q13r to q26r (awareness of 14 services) | Ordinal | Frequency table, mode, median, chi-square goodness of fit |
| R6 | q9r, q11, q12rc | Nominal | Descriptives, chi-square goodness of fit |
| R6 | q10r | Interval (4-point) | One-sample t-test (μ = 2.5) |
| R6 | q31 to q34, q37r | Interval | One-sample t-tests (μ = 3), one per item |

: {tbl-colwidths="[8,32,15,45]"}

## Data Preparation

I used the cleaned file I created in the data preparation assignment (`Case 31 Data_efcu_1_DM_cleaned.sav`). It keeps `q7r`, `q8r`, `q10r`, and `q37r` reverse-coded so higher means better or higher. "No opinion" and "No answer" were already set to missing.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(psych)
library(broom)
library(knitr)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 18))

case31 <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_1_DM_cleaned.sav") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.labelled), as.numeric))
dim(case31)
```

## Extra Recoding for R5 and R6

-   **q13r to q26r:** awareness items flipped so the order runs Unaware < Aware but Have Not Used < Aware and Have Used.
-   **q9r:** statement frequency collapsed into "About right" vs. "Not right".
-   **q11, q12rc:** Yes/No only. "No answer" is treated as missing.

```{r}
aw_levels <- c("Unaware", "Aware but Have Not Used", "Aware and Have Used")

case31 <- case31 |>
  mutate(
    across(q13:q26,
           \(x) factor(4 - x, levels = 1:3, labels = aw_levels, ordered = TRUE),
           .names = "{.col}r"),
    q9r = factor(if_else(q9 == 3, "About right", "Not right"),
                 levels = c("About right", "Not right")),
    q11 = factor(case_match(q11, 1 ~ "Yes", 2 ~ "No", .default = NA_character_),
                 levels = c("Yes", "No")),
    q12rc = factor(case_match(q12, 1 ~ "Yes", 2 ~ "No", .default = NA_character_),
                   levels = c("Yes", "No"))
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
# helper: one-sample t-test summary row
tt <- function(x, mu, label) {
  res <- t.test(x, mu = mu)
  tibble(
    Item = label, n = sum(!is.na(x)), Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), `Test value` = mu,
    t = unname(res$statistic), df = unname(res$parameter),
    p = res$p.value,
    `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", res$conf.int[1], res$conf.int[2])
  )
}
fmt_p <- function(p) if_else(p < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", p))
```

# R1: Why Do People Join the Credit Union? {background-color="aquamarine"}

## R1 Overview

-   **Construct:** Opinion on the savings rate the credit union offers
-   **Operationalization:** q7r (1 = Very Low ... 5 = Very High)
-   **Scale:** Interval (1 to 5 Likert-type)
-   **Statistics:** Descriptive statistics, followed by a one-sample t-test

## R1: Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
case31 |>
  count(q7r) |>
  mutate(
    Opinion = c("Very Low", "Low", "Average", "High", "Very High")[q7r] |> replace_na("Missing"),
    Percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
  ) |>
  select(Opinion, n, Percent) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
describe(case31$q7r) |> kable(digits = 2)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
case31 |>
  filter(!is.na(q7r)) |>
  mutate(q7r = factor(q7r, 1:5, c("Very Low", "Low", "Average", "High", "Very High"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(q7r, fill = q7r)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Opinion on Savings Rate", y = "# of Responses",
       title = "Member Opinions on the Credit Union's Savings Rates")
```

## R1: One-Sample t-Test

-   $H_0: \mu = 3$ (members see the savings rate as "average")
-   $H_A: \mu \neq 3$

```{r}
t.test(case31$q7r, mu = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Insights about R1

-   Most members (65% of all respondents, 70% of those who gave an opinion) say the savings rate is **average**.
-   The sample mean is `r round(mean(case31$q7r, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`, which is not different from 3 (*p* = `r fmt_p(t.test(case31$q7r, mu = 3)$p.value)`).
-   Members see the credit union's savings rate as about average. Savings rates do not stand out as a reason people join.
:::

# R2: Why Do Members Borrow from Other Institutions? {background-color="aquamarine"}

## R2 Overview

-   **Construct:** Reasons to borrow from other financial institutions
-   **Operationalization:** q8r (opinion on loan rates) and q30 (agreement that CU's rates are lower than other institutions)
-   **Scale:** Interval (1 to 5 Likert-type)
-   **Statistics:** Descriptive statistics, followed by one-sample t-tests ($H_0: \mu = 3$)

## R2: Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
bind_rows(
  describe(case31$q8r) |> mutate(item = "q8r: Loan rates (1 = Very Low, 5 = Very High)"),
  describe(case31$q30) |> mutate(item = "q30: CU rates lower than others (1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree)")
) |>
  select(item, n, mean, sd, median, min, max) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
case31 |>
  select(q8r, q30) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(value), fill = item)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~item, labeller = as_labeller(c(q8r = "q8r: Opinion on loan rates", q30 = "q30: CU rates lower than others"))) +
  labs(x = "Response (1 to 5)", y = "# of Responses")
```

## R2: One-Sample t-Tests

```{r}
bind_rows(
  tt(case31$q8r, 3, "q8r: Loan rates"),
  tt(case31$q30, 3, "q30: CU rates lower than others")
) |>
  mutate(p = fmt_p(p)) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Insights about R2

-   Members' opinion of the credit union's loan rates (q8r, *M* = `r round(mean(case31$q8r, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`) is about average and only marginally above 3 (*p* = `r fmt_p(t.test(case31$q8r, mu = 3)$p.value)`).
-   Members neither agree nor disagree that CU rates are lower than competitors' (q30, *M* = `r round(mean(case31$q30), 2)`, *p* = `r fmt_p(t.test(case31$q30, mu = 3)$p.value)`).
-   The credit union does not have a clear rate advantage in members' minds. This may be one reason members look to other institutions when they borrow.
-   **Limit:** The survey has no direct question on why members borrow elsewhere, so this is indirect evidence.
:::

# R5: Awareness of Services {background-color="aquamarine"}

## R5 Overview

-   **Construct:** Awareness of services offered by the credit union
-   **Operationalization:** q13r to q26r (14 services)
-   **Scale:** Ordinal (Unaware < Aware but Have Not Used < Aware and Have Used)
-   **Statistics:** Frequency table, mode, median, chi-square goodness-of-fit test
    -   $H_0$: members are equally spread across the three awareness levels (1/3 each)
    -   $H_A$: the spread is not equal

## R5: Example, Regular Share Account (q13r)

```{r}
tab <- table(case31$q13r)
tab |> as.data.frame() |> rename(Awareness = Var1, n = Freq) |>
  mutate(Percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |> kable()
chisq.test(tab, p = rep(1/3, 3))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
case31 |>
  ggplot(aes(q13r, fill = q13r)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Awareness of Regular Share Account", y = "# of Members")
```

## R5: All 14 Services

```{r}
svc_names <- c(
  q13r = "Regular share account", q14r = "Special subaccounts", q15r = "Christmas club account",
  q16r = "IRA", q17r = "Master credit card", q18r = "Signature loans",
  q19r = "New car loans", q20r = "Late model car loans", q21r = "Older model car loans",
  q22r = "Household goods loans", q23r = "Recreational loans",
  q24r = "Share collateralized loan", q25r = "IRA loans", q26r = "Line of credit loans"
)

aw_long <- case31 |>
  select(q13r:q26r) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "level")

aw_long |>
  count(item, level) |>
  group_by(item) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(cell = paste0(n, " (", pct, "%)")) |>
  select(item, level, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = cell, values_fill = "0 (0%)") |>
  mutate(Service = svc_names[item], .before = 1) |>
  select(Service, all_of(aw_levels)) |>
  kable()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
aw_long |>
  mutate(Service = factor(svc_names[item], levels = rev(svc_names))) |>
  count(Service, level) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, Service, fill = level)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#d95f02", "#7570b3", "#1b9e77")) +
  labs(x = "Percent of Members", y = NULL, fill = "Awareness")
```

## R5: Mode, Median, and Chi-Square Tests

```{r}
r5_tests <- map_dfr(names(svc_names), \(v) {
  x <- case31[[v]]
  ct <- chisq.test(table(x), p = rep(1/3, 3))
  tibble(
    Service = svc_names[[v]],
    Mode = names(which.max(table(x))),
    Median = levels(x)[median(as.numeric(x))],
    `Chi-square` = unname(ct$statistic),
    df = unname(ct$parameter),
    p = fmt_p(ct$p.value)
  )
})
r5_tests |> kable(digits = 1)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Insights about R5

-   For all 14 services, the awareness levels are **not** evenly spread (all *p* < .001), so members' awareness differs clearly across levels.
-   The **regular share account** (q13r), the most basic service, has the highest unawareness (65% unaware). Share-collateralized loans (54%) and IRA loans (61%) also have mostly unaware members.
-   For most loan products (signature, new car, late model car, older model car, household goods, and line of credit loans), most members are **aware but have not used** them.
-   Only the master credit card has a large group of users (about 44%).
-   **Implication:** The credit union has an awareness and usage gap, especially for loans. Promoting loan products and the basic share account could help raise the loan/share ratio.
:::

# R6: Operational Effectiveness {background-color="aquamarine"}

## R6 Overview

-   **Construct:** Attitudes and beliefs about how effectively the credit union is operated
-   **Operationalization and tests:**

| Variable | Meaning | Scale | Test |
|:--|:----------|:------|:------------|
| q9r | Statement frequency is about right | Nominal | Chi-square goodness of fit |
| q10r | Statement accuracy (1 = Poor to 4 = Excellent) | Interval | One-sample t-test (μ = 2.5) |
| q11 | Statements are understandable | Nominal | Chi-square goodness of fit |
| q12rc | Account information is confidential | Nominal | Chi-square goodness of fit |
| q31 to q34 | Confidential, prompt, meets needs, simple applications | Interval | One-sample t-test (μ = 3) |
| q37r | Overall rating (1 = Very Poor to 5 = Excellent) | Interval | One-sample t-test (μ = 3) |

## R6: Nominal Items, Descriptives and Chi-Square

Null hypothesis: responses split 50/50 between the two categories.

```{r}
nom <- tibble(
  Item = c("q9r: Statement frequency", "q11: Statements understandable", "q12rc: Account kept confidential"),
  var = c("q9r", "q11", "q12rc")
)

r6_nom <- map_dfr(nom$var, \(v) {
  tab <- table(case31[[v]])
  ct <- chisq.test(tab, p = c(.5, .5))
  tibble(
    Item = nom$Item[nom$var == v],
    Category1 = paste0(names(tab)[1], ": ", tab[1], " (", round(100 * tab[1] / sum(tab)), "%)"),
    Category2 = paste0(names(tab)[2], ": ", tab[2], " (", round(100 * tab[2] / sum(tab)), "%)"),
    `Chi-square` = unname(ct$statistic), df = unname(ct$parameter), p = fmt_p(ct$p.value)
  )
})
r6_nom |> kable(digits = 1)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
case31 |>
  select(q9r, q11, q12rc) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "resp") |>
  filter(!is.na(resp)) |>
  ggplot(aes(item, fill = resp)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Percent", fill = "Response")
```

## R6: Interval Items, One-Sample t-Tests

```{r}
bind_rows(
  tt(case31$q10r, 2.5, "q10r: Statement accuracy"),
  tt(case31$q31, 3, "q31: CU keeps information confidential"),
  tt(case31$q32, 3, "q32: CU loan processing is prompt"),
  tt(case31$q33, 3, "q33: CU meets members' needs"),
  tt(case31$q34, 3, "q34: CU loan applications are simple"),
  tt(case31$q37r, 3, "q37r: Overall rating")
) |>
  mutate(p = fmt_p(p)) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
case31 |>
  select(q31, q32, q33, q34, q37r) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(item) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            se = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(value)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, item)) +
  geom_col(fill = "lightblue") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = mean - 1.96 * se, xmax = mean + 1.96 * se), height = .2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 5)) +
  labs(x = "Mean (1 to 5, dashed line = neutral point 3)", y = NULL)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Insights about R6

-   **Statements:** Most members (77%) say the frequency of statements is about right, almost all (98%) find them understandable, and the accuracy rating is above the midpoint (*M* = `r round(mean(case31$q10r), 2)` of 4, *p* < .001).
-   **Confidentiality:** 70% of members who answered say their accounts are kept confidential, and agreement that the credit union keeps information confidential is high (q31, *M* = `r round(mean(case31$q31), 2)`).
-   **Service and operations:** Members agree the credit union is prompt (q32, *M* = `r round(mean(case31$q32), 2)`), meets their needs (q33, *M* = `r round(mean(case31$q33), 2)`), and has simple loan applications (q34, *M* = `r round(mean(case31$q34), 2)`). All are significantly above 3 (all *p* < .001).
-   **Overall rating:** Members rate the credit union well overall (q37r, *M* = `r round(mean(case31$q37r, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`, *p* < .001).
-   Operations are viewed favorably, so weak borrowing is probably not caused by how the credit union is run.
:::

# Conclusion {background-color="#a13c65"}

## Summary

-   **R1:** Savings rates are seen as average, so they are not a standout reason for joining.
-   **R2:** Loan rates are also seen as average and not clearly lower than competitors', which may push borrowers elsewhere.
-   **R5:** Awareness is uneven across all 14 services. Many members know about loan products but have not used them, and many do not know about the basic share account.
-   **R6:** Members view operations (statements, confidentiality, promptness, meeting needs, applications) and the credit union overall in a favorable light.
-   **Recommendation:** Focus on promoting loan products and improving the rate message instead of fixing operations.

## Notes and Limits

-   Chi-square goodness-of-fit tests for q9r, q11, and q12rc assume a 50/50 split under the null, which is a simple benchmark.
-   Q2, Q28, and Q29 (direct reasons to join or borrow elsewhere) are not in the data file, so R1 and R2 use the available rate items.
-   The sample has 128 respondents with some missing values (q7r 10, q8r 21, q37r 7).
